item.title: Pimpinella brachycarpa extract attenuates periodontal inflammation by modulating the PI3K/Akt-NF-κB signaling pathway
item.description: CONCLUSION: The present findings indicate that PBE exerts anti-inflammatory and tissue-protective effects in experimental models of periodontitis. The observed effects were associated with suppression of PI3K/Akt-NF-κB signaling. In addition, flavonoid glucuronides identified in PBE exhibited anti-inflammatory activities in vitro. Further studies are required to clarify the contribution of individual constituents to the biological activity of PBE.

item.title: ATG4B-dependent processing of tandem-domain BmLC3 exposes a Tyr136-regulated C-terminal fragment
item.description: Autophagy-related protein 8 (ATG8) family proteins are ubiquitin-like modifiers that undergo ATG4-mediated processing before lipid conjugation. However, the structural and functional diversification of insect ATG8 proteins remains poorly understood. Here, comparative sequence analysis identified a 248-amino-acid LC3C-related protein from the silkworm Bombyx mori (BmLC3) containing two tandem LC3-like regions separated by an internal glycine at position 135 (G135), in addition to the canonical...

item.title: Efficacy of Defibrinogenation Therapy for Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that defibrinogenation treatment is not more effective than other treatments for SSNHL.

item.title: Label-Free YaxAB Nanopore Fingerprinting of Cancer-Associated Single-Residue Bcl-xL Variants
item.description: Resolving cancer-associated protein variants remains difficult when variants share similar molecular masses and folded structures. Conventional assays often require labels or provide ensemble-averaged readouts, limiting their ability to resolve subtle variant differences. Here, a YaxAB nanopore workflow is presented for label-free single-molecule current fingerprinting of wild-type Bcl-xL and the cancer-associated single-residue variants N136K and R165W. Individual Bcl-xL proteins were...

item.title: Nonlinear Electro-Optic Visible Photonic Circuits for Solid-State Quantum Defects
item.description: Integrated visible photonic engines for solid-state quantum defects provide a foundation for scalable quantum networks. While miniaturization is advancing, active manipulation remains limited by the difficulty of achieving simultaneous milliwatt-scale visible light generation and high-contrast modulation. Despite extensive efforts, the concurrent chip-scale realization of nonlinear frequency conversion and fast temporal gating for high-fidelity quantum control has remained elusive. Here, we...

item.title: Patterns of Radiologic Service Utilization and Imaging Expenditure in Supercentenarians in Colombia
item.description: We analyzed radiologic service utilization among Colombian supercentenarians (2014-2023) using administrative health data. Imaging use averaged 3.03 examinations per person annually. General radiology, ultrasound, and computed tomography were the most frequently used modalities. Mean per capita imaging expenditure was 185.22 PPP USD. Compared with centenarians, supercentenarians exhibited a more restricted pattern of imaging utilization, characterized by lower use of advanced imaging modalities...

item.title: Efficacy and Safety of Acellular Dermal Matrix for Prevention of Epidural Fibrosis after Lumbar Fusion Surgery: A Propensity Score-Matched Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: ADM use during lumbar fusion surgery was associated with improved pain control and functional outcomes without additional safety concerns. ADM may be a useful option for preventing epidural fibrosis. Further prospective studies are warranted.

item.title: Independent Association Between Lumbar Intervertebral Disc Degeneration and Fatty Degeneration of Paravertebral Muscles
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Fatty degeneration of paravertebral muscles was significantly associated with degenerative changes of intervertebral discs in the lumbar spine, even considering age, sex, osteoporosis, and shift work.

item.title: AI-assisted 3D thoracic body composition analysis identifies candidate imaging markers associated with overall survival in older patients with lung cancer receiving radiotherapy
item.description: CONCLUSION: AI-assisted analysis of routine radiotherapy simulation CT identified IAI and TMF as candidate body-composition imaging markers associated with overall survival in this clinically heterogeneous cohort. The findings are exploratory and require independent evaluation in larger, clinically characterized cohorts before clinical use.

item.title: Dacomitinib With or Without Dose Titration in Treatment-Naive Advanced EGFR-Mutated NSCLC - Primary Analysis of the ATORG-003 Phase 2 Trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: ATORG-003 prospectively revealed that dacomitinib with dose titration is a viable strategy in advanced EGFR-mutated NSCLC, maintaining efficacy while improving tolerability. Dacomitinib has substantial intracranial activity and high rates of T790M resistance, making it suitable for sequential treatment approaches.

item.title: Dual-pathway processing of AI-generated Chinese ink painting: evidence from eye-tracking, EEG, and artistic expertise
item.description: AI-driven generative art is changing the scope of artistic creation, but the principles behind its aesthetics and the perception of its outcomes remain relatively unexplored, especially concerning culturally specific art forms. The present study investigates how viewers cognitively, affectively, and evaluatively process AI-generated Chinese ink paintings, and whether artistic expertise moderates these responses. We introduce the concept of expressive expansion as a viewer-perceived psychological...

item.title: Coexisting adrenal hemangioma and aldosterone-producing micronodule presented as adrenal incidentaloma
item.description: Adrenal hemangiomas are rare benign vascular tumors, an uncommon cause of adrenal incidentalomas. We report a patient with coexisting adrenal hemangioma and aldosterone-producing micronodules within the same adrenal gland. A 67-year-old man was referred for an incidental left adrenal mass. Noncontrast computed tomography revealed a 1.6 × 1.4 cm lesion with an unenhanced attenuation value of 40 Hounsfield units. Initial hormonal evaluation was unremarkable except for an elevated...

item.title: Amivantamab plus chemotherapy vs. chemotherapy in participants with EGFR-mutant advanced non-small cell lung cancer after progression on osimertinib: a MARIPOSA-2 analysis of the Asian subgroup
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Amivantamab-chemotherapy demonstrated superior PFS vs. chemotherapy in Asian patients. Amivantamab-chemotherapy provides an effective option for patients whose disease had progressed on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors.

item.title: Recent advances and perspectives on multicomponent metallic electrocatalysts for water splitting and related reactions
item.description: Compositionally engineered metallic nanostructured catalysts have received burgeoning attention in electrochemical energy conversion. This growing interest stems from their tunable atomic structures, controlled stoichiometry, diverse coordination environments, enhanced orbital interactions, and high electronic and structural flexibility. Alloys are broadly classified into two categories: intermetallic compounds and solid-solutions based on their structure, phase and atomic arrangement. These...

item.title: Emergence of the GI-23 lineage of infectious bronchitis virus in Brazilian backyard poultry
item.description: Infectious bronchitis virus (IBV) remains a major threat to poultry production worldwide, with the GI-23 lineage emerging as one of the most epidemiologically relevant variants in recent years. Although GI-23 has been reported in Brazilian commercial poultry, its occurrence and genomic characteristics in backyard poultry remain poorly understood. This study investigated the molecular epidemiology and evolutionary features of IBV circulating in backyard poultry from São Paulo State, Brazil....

item.title: Pathway Engineering Enables Durable Iridium-Free Acidic Water Oxidation
item.description: The pursuit of noble metal-free alternatives to iridium for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is critically impeded by a pervasive activity-stability trade-off, wherein non-precious metals undergo rapid oxidative dissolution under operating potentials. Here, we report a lutetium-stabilized cobalt oxide catalyst (Lu(0.08)Co(2.92)O(4)) designed through site-specific electronic modulation, achieving a synergistic enhancement of both activity and stability in acidic OER for proton exchange...

item.title: Long-term National Trends in the Prevalence of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and the Association with Social Determinants of Health in Korean Adults, 2007-2024
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: T2DM prevalence has increased over time, and a high cumulative burden of SDOH remains consistently associated with this prevalence, highlighting the need for equity-focused public health strategies.

item.title: Computed Tomographic Findings of Hepatic Rupture Associated With Amyloidosis in a Young Siamese Cat
item.description: A 3-year-old neutered male Siamese cat with chronic anorexia showed anemia and elevated liver enzyme levels. Ultrasonography disclosed multiple diffusely heterogeneous hepatic lesions and peritoneal effusion, which was identified as hemoabdomen upon fluid analysis. Computed tomography showed finger-like hypoattenuation extending from the left hepatic margin with focal margin loss in the delayed phase, suggesting hepatic rupture. Infiltrative hepatic diseases were considered, and amyloidosis was...

item.title: A practical guide to automated test assembly for educational evaluation in health professions: a demonstration using the R package ROI
item.description: Automated test assembly (ATA) using mixed-integer programming (MIP) is standard practice in international testing organizations, but detailed and accessible practical guidelines remain scarce for health professions assessment. This study introduces the mathematical foundations of MIP-based ATA and provides a step-by-step tutorial demonstrating its implementation with the open-source R package ROI and the HiGHS solver. We constructed a modified 928-item pool with empirical item parameters from...

item.title: Machine Learning-Guided Identification of Madecassoside as a Potential RAD51 Modulator That Sensitizes Breast Cancer Cells to Cisplatin
item.description: Homologous recombination (HR) is an essential pathway for preserving the genomic stability of cells by repairing DNA damage, especially double-strand breaks and interstrand crosslinks. RAD51 recombinase plays a central role in the HR pathway, and when DNA damage occurs, RAD51 binds to single-stranded DNA at the cleavage site to form a helical nucleoprotein filament. Therefore, pharmacological inhibition of RAD51 is emerging as an attractive strategy to block the repair mechanisms of cancer cells...

item.title: Temperature-dependent effects of post-exercise cold-water immersion on recovery: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: On average, CWI was associated with reductions in DOMS, CK, and Mb, although substantial heterogeneity and wide prediction intervals indicate that these effects may not be consistently reproduced across settings. Numerically larger reductions in DOMS were observed at approximately 10-15 °C than at ≈5 °C, but neither subgroup analysis nor meta-regression confirmed a temperature-dependent effect. No water-temperature range can currently be considered superior.

item.title: Enantioselective synthesis of β-aryl-β-acyl esters as unsymmetrical 1,4-dicarbonyl compounds via oxidative aryl rearrangement using λ3-perchrolate iodane
item.description: In synthetic chemistry, structurally diverse unsymmetrical 1,4-dicarbonyl compounds are important, and general strategies for their asymmetric synthesis, particularly for β-aryl-substituted β-acyl esters, are scarce. Therefore, this study presents an enantioselective oxidative aryl rearrangement of α-styryl esters using a combination of a hypervalent iodine(iii) reagent and Mg(ClO(4))(2) as a Lewis acid to provide chiral β-aryl-β-formyl and β-aryl-β-acyl esters in high yields with excellent...

item.title: Frontal-striatal-thalamic circuit dysfunction and inferential processing between internal representations and external events across the psychosis spectrum
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This conceptual model may provide a novel perspective on the information-processing mechanisms, particularly inferential processing, and their alterations across high-risk clinical states for psychosis, including ARMS/APS and broader Clinical High At Risk Mental States (CHARMS) concept.

item.title: Evaluation of Preoperative Factors Associated with Early Postoperative Neurological Outcome in the Treatment of Metastatic Spinal Tumors
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The spinal cord compression site was a neurological prognostic factor for early postoperative neurological outcome. Even in cases with an ASIA grade of B or C, neurological improvement in the early postoperative period was anticipated if the compression site was posterior-only.

item.title: Premature stop codons in inlA reduce Caco-2 cell invasion by Listeria monocytogenes and contribute to serotype bias in human clinical isolates
item.description: Listeria monocytogenes is a highly lethal foodborne pathogen that exhibits strain-dependent differences in virulence. Infection begins with traversal of the intestinal barrier through a two-step process involving adhesion to intestinal epithelial cells followed by intracellular invasion. In this study, Caco-2 cells were used to investigate these early infection events in 25 Japanese L. monocytogenes isolates (9 human clinical, 14 food-derived, and 2 environmental isolates) and 1 reference...

item.title: Gut microbiota alters the Th1/Th2 balance and aggravates food-allergic enteropathy in a mouse model
item.description: In non-IgE-mediated food allergy, food protein-induced enteropathy (FPE) can be evoked by the Th2 response. Some reports show that either Th2-biased immune responses or gut microbial dysbiosis can exacerbate food-allergic gastrointestinal inflammation. Nevertheless, it remains unclear whether gut microbiota directly affect Th2-biased immune responses involving FPE. To address this issue, we used OVA23-3 × BALB/cA mice, which is an FPE-like model. Feeding the mice an egg-white diet (EW) induced...

item.title: Prognostic impact of immune-related adverse events in non-completers of durvalumab consolidation therapy for non-small cell lung cancer: a single-center retrospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: One-year durvalumab completion remains the primary clinical objective. In patients discontinuing early, irAE onset was associated with a potential prognostic signal after controlling for time-varying bias; however, these findings represent cautious, hypothesis-generating observations requiring prospective multi-center validation.

item.title: Associations between autobiographical characteristics of past and future events, anhedonia and anticipatory pleasure: a cross-sectional study in a community sample of adolescents
item.description: Impairments in autobiographical characteristics of Episodic Future Thinking (EFT) and Autobiographical (AM), such as reduced specificity, level of detail, and mental imagery, are associated with stress-related mental health problems in adults, including depression. The current study aims to identify which cognitive and emotional autobiographical characteristics, including objectively-rated level of specificity and autobiographical detail, predict unique variance in anhedonia and anticipatory...

item.title: Immunosuppression and Long-term Survival After Single Living-donor Lobar Lung Transplantation From the Same Donor as Prior Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: An All-Japan Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this highly selected case series, acceptable long-term survival was observed after single LDLLT from the same donor as prior HSCT under reduced immunosuppression, and immunosuppression was successfully withdrawn in 3 patients.

item.title: Temporal changes in clinical practices for patients considered clinically brain dead: a single-center cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The opportunity for organ donation discussion increased over time among patients considered clinically brain dead, while the proportion of families consenting to donation remained relatively stable. This increase occurred alongside the progressive development of structured multidisciplinary processes, although their contribution to the observed temporal trend cannot be determined from this descriptive study.

item.title: Anterior segment optical coherence tomography-guided management of capsular contraction and anterior-posterior capsular adhesion after congenital cataract surgery: a case report
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Intraoperative AS-OCT may serve as a useful adjunct in the management of postoperative capsular adhesion after congenital cataract surgery by helping surgeons identify the dissection plane and guide intraoperative decision-making, particularly when conventional microscopic visualization is limited.

item.title: Comparative accuracy of automated carbohydrate estimation using NutriDish and ChatGPT-5 against dietitian-derived reference values
item.description: CONCLUSION: NutriDish demonstrated good agreement with dietitian-derived carbohydrate estimates, highlighting its potential to aid carbohydrate counting in individuals treated with insulin. Future studies should evaluate real-world clinical usability, integration into diabetes self-management ecosystems and impact on long-term glycemic control.

item.title: The Future of Newly Diagnosed HIV Cases in Iran Through 2030: A Mixed-Methods Trend Impact Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: The scenario projections represent conditional future trajectories based on specified assumptions about the impact of different key drivers, The scenarios illustrate substantial uncertainty in the future number of newly diagnosed HIV cases in Iran, with scenario estimates ranging from approximately a 50% decrease to a 100% increase relative to the baseline projection.

item.title: Barriers and Facilitators to Participation in the Employees' Health Cohort Study of Iran (EHCSIR): A Qualitative Content Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Organizational, logistical, and perceptual factors significantly influence participation in occupational health cohorts. Improving management, infrastructure, communication, and institutional trust can enhance recruitment and retention in EHCSIR and inform similar strategies both in Iran and internationally.

item.title: Burden of typhoid fever in primary and hospital care in Indonesia: a serial cross-sectional study using national health insurance (BPJS Kesehatan) data, 2015-2023
item.description: BACKGROUND: Despite Indonesia's high typhoid burden, subnational prevalence data remain sparse, limiting risk mapping and targeted interventions. We characterised trends in typhoid presentation in primary care and hospital settings, described geographic patterns, and identified factors associated with hospitalisation.

item.title: Patient-derived stem cell models of brain endothelial-neuron interactions in early course psychosis
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Early-course psychosis (ECP) exhibits marked heterogeneity in illness trajectories, with a substantial subset of individuals developing progressive symptomatic, cognitive, and functional decline. Although growing evidence implicates blood-brain barrier (BBB) and neurovascular unit (NVU) dysfunction in psychosis spectrum disorders, direct links between longitudinal clinical trajectories and disease-related cellular phenotypes remain insufficiently characterized.

item.title: Which Domains of Cognition in Older Adults Are Affected by Sleep Duration? A Scoping Review
item.description: CONCLUSION: This review highlights cognitive domains affected by inadequate sleep in older adults and emphasizes the need for more research on gender-specific differences in sleep duration. It also pointed out a gap in understanding the link between sleep duration and social cognition, emphasizing the need for further studies in this area.

item.title: <sup>18</sup>F-AlF-NOTA-FAPI-04 PET/CT as a complementary tool for detecting occult signet-ring cell gastric adenocarcinoma when FDG imaging is inconclusive: a case report
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: ^(18)F-FAPI PET/CT can provide complementary biological and diagnostic information when ^(18)F-FDG imaging is inconclusive, particularly in stroma‑rich gastric cancers with signet‑ring cell features. In this patient, FAPI PET/CT enabled targeted biopsy and demonstrated treatment response, suggesting its potential value in clinical management. Larger prospective studies are warranted to further define the role of ^(18)F-FAPI PET/CT in the diagnostic algorithm of occult primary...

item.title: A hypoxia-responsive calixarene supramolecular system enables redox-regulated matrix remodeling for postmenopausal osteoporosis
item.description: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) is characterized by progressive bone loss driven by excessive osteoclast activity, impaired osteogenesis, and maladaptive remodeling of the bone microenvironment. Although raloxifene (RLX) is clinically approved for PMOP, its therapeutic potential is constrained by limited bone selectivity and systemic adverse effects. Here, we report a hypoxia-responsive, bone-targeted supramolecular system (RLX@PnAC4A) that integrates site-selective drug delivery with redox...

item.title: Atractylenolide III attenuates age-related vertebral bone loss by suppressing macrophage inflammation and osteoclastogenesis
item.description: Age-related bone loss is driven in part by inflammatory remodeling of the bone marrow niche, which promotes macrophage activation and osteoclastogenesis. Atractylenolide III (AT-III) is a chemically defined sesquiterpene lactone with anti-inflammatory activity, but its skeletal effects in natural aging remain unclear. Bone marrow cells and macrophages from young and aged mice were evaluated by flow cytometry, ELISA, immunostaining, TRAP staining, RT-qPCR, and immunoblotting....

item.title: From respiratory viral infection to persistent cough hypersensitivity: neuroimmune regulation and therapeutic implications of P2X3/TRP ion-channel targets
item.description: Respiratory viral infections are increasingly recognized as important drivers of persistent airway symptoms and exacerbations in chronic lung disease. Post-infectious cough (PIC), particularly after upper respiratory tract infection, represents one of the most frequent causes of subacute cough and a mechanistically complex sequela in which cough hypersensitivity syndrome (CHS) plays a central pathophysiological role. Beyond increased cough frequency, patients with PIC frequently exhibit...

item.title: A Decade of Discovery: Methodological Innovation, Capacity Building, and Global Leadership in Hidden Population Research in Iran
item.description: CONCLUSION: The Iranian population size estimation program demonstrates how sustained collaboration between modelling and public health researchers can generate evidence, build national capacity, strengthen institutions, and support public health policy. The program provides a model for developing similar initiatives in other settings.

item.title: Cellular signaling meets bacterial infection: the integrative role of STAT3
item.description: STAT3 is a central mediator of pro-survival signaling within the STAT family, functioning through both canonical transcriptional activity and noncanonical mechanisms. As a pleiotropic regulator, STAT3 integrates cytokine, growth factor, and stress signals to coordinate diverse cellular processes, including epithelial architecture, T cell development, macrophage polarization, apoptosis, metabolism, and inflammation-associated wound healing. This integrative capacity positions STAT3 as a critical...

item.title: Case Report: Tubal recanalization and short-term re-pregnancy after repeat ligation following two cesarean sections
item.description: CONCLUSION: Although pregnancy rates after tubal recanalization can reach 80%-90%, repeat ligation following recanalization does not guarantee absolute contraceptive efficacy. Spontaneous re-canalization with subsequent pregnancy remains possible. This case highlights the importance of standardized surgical technique, long-term follow-up, and postoperative contraceptive counseling, particularly in patients with a history of tubal surgery.

item.title: Atypical Extramedullary Acute Myeloid Leukemia in Infancy: Bilateral Testicular Swelling and Scalp Lesions at Diagnosis
item.description: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is rare in infancy, with monocytic subtypes such as acute myelomonocytic leukemia often demonstrating extramedullary involvement. This report describes a 10-month-old male infant presenting with firm bilateral testicular enlargement and multiple parietal scalp nodules, accompanied by leukocytosis and circulating blasts in peripheral blood. Bone marrow examination confirmed French-American-British (FAB) M4 AML. Scrotal ultrasound demonstrated heterogeneous masses, and...

item.title: MambaGLA-NPC: a 3D framework integrating CNN and state space models for robust multi-center nasopharyngeal carcinoma segmentation
item.description: CONCLUSION: MambaGLA-NPC is the first Mamba-based 3D NPC segmentation framework that effectively balances local-global feature integration with linear complexity, achieving superior accuracy and generalization across multi-center MRI data while maintaining high efficiency.

item.title: Epidemiological update on spatial and space-time clusters of African swine fever in the Philippines
item.description: African swine fever (ASF), particularly the highly contagious Genotype II strain, is a transboundary viral disease causing up to 100% mortality in swine and threatening food security across the Asia-Pacific region. Since 2019, control strategies in the Philippines have relied on depopulation and strict administrative zoning to limit contiguous, land-based spread. However, the long-term effectiveness of these approaches within the country's fragmented archipelagic landscape remains poorly...

item.title: A pilot study of invasive vagus nerve stimulation in Chinese patients with Alzheimer's disease: preliminary results on safety, cognition, and biomarkers
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with no curative therapies, and vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) has emerged as a promising neuromodulatory approach. This prospective, open-label pilot study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and preliminary cognitive, psychological, inflammatory, and AD biomarker effects of invasive VNS (iVNS) in Chinese AD patients.

item.title: Factors Associated With Skilled Birth Attendance Among Internally Displaced Women in Mogadishu, Somalia: A Community-Based Cross-Sectional Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: SBA was very low among displaced women in these camps. ANC attendance and basic education were associated with SBA. Given the cross-sectional design, the sampling of selected camps, and imprecise subgroup estimates, these associations should not be interpreted as causal or generalized to all displaced populations in Somalia.

item.title: Pulsed field ablation for persistent atrial fibrillation with atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia under tubeless general anesthesia: a case report
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: AVRT is a type of supraventricular tachycardia caused by the presence of an accessory pathway due to congenital structural abnormalities. Our case reports an AVRT occurrence during PFA for AF and provides significant evidence that PFA is effective and safe for accessory pathway ablation during AF ablation.

item.title: Age-related differences in behavioral and brain predictors of parkinsonism in autistic adults
item.description: Autistic adults experience lifelong motor differences and may have increased vulnerability to parkinsonism, yet behavioral and neuroanatomical correlates of motor challenges across adulthood remain poorly understood. We examined cross-sectional behavioral and motor-related brain region morphology in autistic (n = 123) and non-autistic (n = 102) adults aged 18-71 years using the Parkinsonism Screening Questionnaire (PSQ), Adult Repetitive Behavior Questionnaire-2 (RBQ-2A), finger tapping, and...

item.title: Beyond physical isolation: behavioral correlates and potential neurobiological mechanisms of functional social isolation
item.description: Functional Social Isolation (FSI) describes a proposed form of social disconnection in the digital era, wherein individuals are physically co-present yet psychologically detached during pervasive digital immersion. This review examines how everyday digital immersion may contribute to persistent social disengagement, outlines its behavioral correlates and potential neurobiological pathways, and discusses its implications for public health and behavioral psychology. By synthesizing emerging...

item.title: The impact of male circumcision on risk of HIV infection in sub-Saharan Africa: a household fixed-effects analysis of 279,351 men from 29 countries
item.description: CONCLUSION: Male circumcision was associated with a significant reduction in the risk of HIV infection in sub-Saharan Africa over the past two decades. Increased political and financial commitment to VMMC could likely lead to further reductions in HIV prevalence, especially when rolled out as a HIV prevention option in combination with other interventions.

item.title: Real-world deployment and longitudinal evaluation of a human-in-the-loop telemedicine communication support system
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate the potential of automated communication support systems to assist routine telemedicine workflows while maintaining human oversight of patient communication. At the same time, practical challenges related to system integration, data timeliness, and context awareness remain important considerations for successful deployment in clinical environments.

item.title: Context-dependent value of HLA class I diversity in advanced non-small cell lung cancer treated with immune checkpoint blockade
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In advanced NSCLC treated predominantly with first line chemo-immunotherapy, composite HLA class I diversity does not improve outcome prediction beyond established biomarkers. Locus-specific HLA metrics, particularly HLA-B, may warrant further investigation.

item.title: Clinical spectrum and genotype-phenotype correlations of MT-CYB-associated mitochondrial disease: from the m.15045G > A variant to the broader disease landscape
item.description: CONCLUSION: Our findings provide further evidence for the pathogenicity of m.15045G > A and broaden its associated clinical and metabolic features. Tissue-specific distribution of MT-CYB variants showed an association with clinical phenotype, while other genetic and functional factors may collectively contribute to phenotypic variability.

item.title: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma as a second malignancy in a patient with cervical squamous cell carcinoma following chemoradiotherapy: a case report
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Radiotherapy, cisplatin-based chemotherapy, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) activation, age-related immunosenescence, poorly controlled long-term diabetes mellitus (DM) and SARS-CoV-2 infection-related immunosuppression may have collectively contributed to lymphomagenesis. This case highlights the critical need for sustained long-term follow-up in cervical cancer patients, especially those burdened with concurrent chronic diseases. In the setting of unexplained fever or lymphadenopathy,...

item.title: Sleep disturbance and its associations with night shift work, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms among urban operation-supporting workers: a cross-sectional study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Sleep disturbance was prevalent among urban operation-supporting occupational groups. Night shift work and anxiety symptoms were associated with sleep disturbance, with anxiety showing the most stable association. Depressive symptoms showed a weaker, model-dependent association. Sleep and mental health interventions may need to consider occupational context.

item.title: SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence and extent of infection under-ascertainment in seven regions of Uzbekistan: a population-based serosurvey, May-July 2022
item.description: Accurate estimation of SARS-CoV-2 transmission was limited in many settings by incomplete diagnostic testing and case reporting. We conducted a population-based cross-sectional serosurvey in seven regions of Uzbekistan between May and July 2022 to estimate SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence, describe self-reported vaccination coverage, and assess the implications for routine surveillance. A two-stage cluster sampling design was used to randomly select polyclinic catchment areas and registered residents...

item.title: From Concept to Implementation: A Policy and Standards Roadmap for a Global Medical Record System for Travelers with Chronic Disease
item.description: International travel by people with multimorbidity and polypharmacy is increasing, and clinicians who treat these patients abroad seldom have access to accurate and current information about them. Mechanisms for cross-border exchange do exist: the International Patient Summary (IPS), European cross-border health services, and national patient portals all move summary clinical data between jurisdictions. What none of them yet provides is automated abstraction of decades of longitudinal records...

item.title: Postoperative chylothorax associated with lymphatic channels around the azygos arch after right upper lobectomy: a case report
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This case describes an intraoperative observation of two lymphatic channels around the azygos arch during right superior mediastinal lymphadenectomy. Because no dedicated lymphatic imaging or formal anatomical confirmation was performed, the complete lymphatic course and anatomical classification of these channels remain uncertain. This observation is hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as definitive confirmation of a thoracic duct anomaly.

item.title: Understanding histotripsy ablation safety: a systematic review of pre-clinical and clinical adverse events
item.description: Histotripsy is the first cavitation-based ablation modality. Given limited clinical experience, synthesis of pre-clinical and early clinical data is essential to guide safe adoption. A PubMed and SCOPUS search was performed focused on pre-clinical and clinical adverse events (AEs) from Histotripsy ablation of parenchymal tissues in vivo (n = 141 total studies, n = 27 clinical reports). Early data suggest an acceptable acute safety profile in select settings; however, reports of serious AEs...

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Common Data Elements for Preclinical High-Frequency Oscillations in Epilepsy
item.description: Normal brain function relies on coordinated oscillations within and across neural circuits. In epilepsy, disruption of these oscillations may reflect pathological excitability associated with seizure generation and/or the emergence of comorbidities. Among these oscillatory activities, high-frequency oscillations (HFOs, typically within 80-500 Hz) are increasingly considered promising electrophysiological biomarkers of epileptogenicity. Preclinical models provide a powerful platform for...

item.title: PAH-associated health risk from ultrafine particles: an urban field study
item.description: Ultrafine particles (UFPs) are airborne particulate matter with diameters less than 100 nm. UFPs present in urban atmospheres pose a significant public health issue because they usually carry harmful substances, including toxic metals and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). Prolonged exposure to urban UFPs may result in cumulative deposition of these harmful substances in the human respiratory system, elevating the likelihood of adverse respiratory outcomes. Thus, studying UFP respiratory...

item.title: "Am I a candidate for magic mushrooms?" A mystery shopper study of Oregon psilocybin service centers
item.description: CONCLUSION: Oregon's regulated model appears clinically cautious, while facing high costs for clients, facilitators, and service centers that limit scalability.

item.title: A Difference-in-Differences Analysis of Low-Value Opioid Utilization for Acute Low Back Pain, 2019-2021
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The decline in low-value opioid utilization for acute LBP was accelerated during 2020-2021. Utilization was consistently higher in rural than nonrural areas. Findings highlight the need for targeted interventions and policy to reduce low-value opioid utilization, especially in rural areas to ensure equitable, high-value care for acute pain.

item.title: pH-responsive Zn<sup>2+</sup>-coordinated gellan gum/γ-polyglutamic acid hydrogel microspheres as functional biomaterials for intra-articular delivery: physicochemical design, smart release, and chondroprotective performance in osteoarthritis
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive degradation of the articular cartilage matrix, pain-related functional impairment, and a paucity of effective disease-modifying therapies. Curculigoside (Cur), a bioactive compound isolated from Curculigo orchioides, possesses anti-inflammatory and tissue-protective properties; however, its direct intra-articular application is hampered by insufficient local retention and limited sustained action.

item.title: Length of Hospitalization of Patients with Spinal Trauma Caused by Motor Vehicle Accidents: Retrospective Study from a Level 1 Trauma Center
item.description: CONCLUSION: Advanced age, polytrauma, and injury to thoracic or multiple spinal regions are significant predictors of mortality and extended hospitalization in TSF patients post-MVA. The findings highlight the importance of early risk stratification and individualized management strategies in trauma patients, particularly those of advanced age or with multiple injuries. Further multicenter studies incorporating long-term functional outcomes are warranted to inform comprehensive trauma care...

item.title: Nucleotide Metabolic Reprogramming in Sepsis: From Immune-Cell Fate to Organ Injury and Precision Therapeutics
item.description: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by concurrent inflammation, immunosuppression, endothelial dysfunction and metabolic failure. Although current immunometabolic research primarily focuses on glycolysis, mitochondrial respiration and lipid metabolism, nucleotide metabolism links biosynthesis, redox homeostasis, epigenetic regulation and extracellular danger signalling. This Review synthesizes evidence for altered purine and pyrimidine synthesis, ribonucleotide reduction,...

item.title: Associations between quantitative ocular surface features and CT morphology of the levator palpebrae superioris complex in patients with thyroid eye disease and upper eyelid retraction: a cross-sectional study
item.description: CONCLUSION: In this selected cohort of patients, LPSC enlargement was associated with reduced meibomian gland vagueness. The relationship between LPSC enlargement and increased TMH appeared to be indirect and may involve proptosis.

item.title: Building recovery capital: co-creating an assets-based community engagement toolkit for people accessing drug and alcohol treatment services
item.description: CONCLUSION: The ABCE toolkit offers a scalable, recovery-oriented framework for strengthening recovery capital through increased engagement with community assets and embedding asset-based practice within treatment and recovery services.

item.title: Pyrochar versus hydrochar: contrasting modulation of soil bacterial communities under severe nitrate-dominated acid rain stress in a Quercus acutissima plantation
item.description: Nitrate-dominated acid rain (NAR) has become an increasingly prevalent component of contemporary atmospheric deposition and can profoundly alter soil bacterial communities in forest ecosystems. Biochar amendment has been proposed as a potential strategy for modifying soil conditions under acid deposition stress. However, the material-dependent effects of pyrochar (PC) and hydrochar (HC) on bacterial community responses under severe NAR stress remain unclear. Here, a field experiment was...

item.title: Designing evaluation infrastructure for psychedelic harm reduction at events: a methodological framework with formative mixed-methods field application
item.description: Psychedelic and other psychoactive substance use is increasing in non-clinical environments, including music festivals, concerts, and other large-scale gatherings. As psychedelic use expands beyond clinical settings, policymakers, healthcare systems, event operators, and researchers require evidence-informed frameworks for understanding and responding to psychoactive-related distress in naturalistic environments. Despite the growing presence of psychedelic harm reduction services, few studies...

item.title: Zhuyu pill relieves cholestasis in rats by modulating the expression of lncRNAs and circRNAs
item.description: CONCLUSION: ZYP dose-dependently improved biochemical and histopathological parameters in cholestatic rats. This effect is closely related to the roles of lncRNAs and circRNAs in regulating lipid metabolism and inflammation-related pathways. Several candidate ceRNA pairs were preliminarily screened, yet further experimental validation is warranted.

item.title: The weight of pills: medication use and fall incidence in Saudi community-dwelling adults aged 50 years and older: a 10-month longitudinal study
item.description: CONCLUSION: This exploratory study suggests a possible association between baseline polypharmacy and fall incidence over a follow-up period of up to 10 months among community-dwelling Saudi adults aged 50 years and older. However, these findings were based on a small polypharmacy subgroup (n = 14) and include only six events, so they should be interpreted with caution. These findings may support further investigation of medication and polypharmacy screening as part of broader fall-risk...

item.title: Unearthing a fungal giant: Dianjunaceae fam. nov., a novel Paleocene lineage of Xylariales harboring Dianjunus rex gen. et sp. nov
item.description: During mycological surveys in Yunnan Province, China, specimens of a fungus producing massive, upright stromata up to 50 cm high and individually 2.2 kg in weight were sampled. Through an integrative taxonomic approach combining detailed morphology, multilocus phylogeny [internal transcribed spacer (ITS), large subunit ribosomal DNA (LSU), RNA polymerase II subunit 2 (RPB2), and beta-tubulin (TUB2)], and phylogenomic analyses, this fungus is proposed as the new species Dianjunus rex gen. et sp....

item.title: Clemastine alleviates Parkinson's disease pathology by activating the AMPK/mTOR pathway and enhancing autophagic flux
item.description: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a debilitating neurodegenerative disorder with no available cure, underscoring the urgent need for novel therapeutics. This study employed the comprehensive bioinformatic analyses and the experimental models to investigate the potential of clemastine (CLE) for PD treatment. Bioinformatics identified 12 distinct cell subtypes and 577 differentially expressed genes in dopaminergic neurons (DaNs), along with 167 potential PD-relevant CLE targets. A significant...

item.title: From metric to model: a five-stage pipeline for building and sustaining valid AI predictive systems in consumer neuroscience
item.description: The application of machine learning to consumer neuroscience has made it possible, in principle, to predict consumer responses from media assets alone. However, the pursuit of model sophistication has outpaced attention to a foundational constraint: the quality of any predictive artificial intelligence (AI) system is bounded by the quality of the neurophysiological and biometric data used to train it, and by the rigor of the modeling procedures applied to those data. This article argues that...

item.title: Quantum Hall antidot as a fractional coulombmeter
item.description: The ability to detect the fractionally charged quasiparticles that arise in the fractional quantum Hall regime is of fundamental importance for probing their quantum properties. Although electronic interferometers have successfully probed their statistical properties, interpreting the results is often complicated by bulk-edge interactions. Antidots-tunable hills in the potential landscape in the device-are particularly valuable in this context, as they overcome the geometric limitations of...

item.title: Commentary: Pembrolizumab-induced type-1 diabetes mellitus: clinical characteristics, therapeutic strategies, and prognosis from a retrospective analysis of 43 published cases
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Source-based morphometry analyses yield associations between large-scale structural brain networks and psychopathic traits in incarcerated adolescents
item.description: Studies commonly report that youth with elevated psychopathic traits exhibit deficits within limbic and paralimbic regions, including reduced gray matter volume (GMV) in the amygdala, orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), and temporal pole. However, studies have also reported additional structural abnormalities in regions extending beyond limbic and paralimbic regions among youth with elevated psychopathic traits, including the middle frontal gyrus (MFG), inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), precuneus, inferior...

item.title: Electronic Health Record Integration of a Calculator for Cesarean Risk During Labor Induction
item.description: CONCLUSION: Behaviorally designed EHR integration of a cesarean risk calculator for labor induction was associated with significant increases in calculator utilization and documentation of patient counseling. This model could be applied to other evidence-based health-related risk calculators.

item.title: Synergistic effects and molecular mechanisms of pirfenidone combined with EGFR-TKIs in non-small cell lung cancer
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: PFD enhances the efficacy of EGFR-TKIs through a dual mechanism: first, by specifically inhibiting the p38γ-mediated PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway, and second, by activating a p38γ-independent autophagy pathway. The activation of the p38γ-mediated PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway may represent a key mechanism underlying OS resistance. This study provides the first evidence that PFD can restore drug sensitivity in OS-resistant cells, offering valuable experimental support for its potential...

item.title: Curve walking gait analysis using depth camera and machine learning for detecting cognitive impairment
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Early detection of cognitive impairment (CI), including MCI and Alzheimer's disease (AD), remains limited by the invasiveness and cost of current diagnostic tools. While gait analysis is a promising alternative, most studies focus on straight-path walking, which may miss subtle motor-cognitive deficits. We hypothesized that curve walking-especially under dual-task (DT) conditions-would better expose early CI-related changes. Combined with machine learning, this approach offers a...

item.title: Safety signals and CMV-related events reported during letermovir therapy: a FAERS database study
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study identified safety signals reported with letermovir involving hematological, cardiac, hepatic, renal, infectious, and transplantation-related events. CMV-related signals may reflect breakthrough infection. These findings require validation in clinical studies.

item.title: Saccharomyces boulardii reduces food intake and attenuates weight gain in diet-induced obese mice: links to gut microbial, metabolic, and immune remodeling
item.description: INTRODUCTION: The gut microbiome is a key regulator of metabolic homeostasis and contributes to obesity progression through effects on immune signaling, gut barrier integrity, and systemic inflammation. Microbiome-targeted strategies are therefore being explored as complementary approaches to conventional weight-loss therapies. Here, we investigated whether the probiotic yeast Saccharomyces boulardii modulates the gut-immune-metabolic axis in diet-induced obesity (DIO).

item.title: Multimodal digital assessment of early recovery after chest tube omission in early-stage lung cancer patients undergoing wedge resection: a post hoc analysis of a prospective cohort
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: After wedge resection, omission of routine chest tube drainage was associated with a more favorable early patient-reported recovery, whereas physiologic differences were modest. Multimodal digital assessment may offer a practical and patient-centered approach to postoperative monitoring after minimally invasive thoracic surgery.

item.title: Early prediction of 3-month functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke: an explainable model based on routine clinical data
item.description: CONCLUSION: An explainable model based on routinely collected clinical data showed good discrimination and calibration in internal validation for predicting 3-month functional outcome after AIS. Independent external validation is required before the model can be considered for clinical application.

item.title: Retrospective real-world associations between EGFR alterations and furmonertinib outcomes in advanced non-small cell lung cancer
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This retrospective real-world cohort suggests that EGFR subtypes and multiple concurrent genomic alterations are associated with survival outcomes under furmonertinib treatment.

item.title: Robotic-assisted beating heart surgery: a comprehensive review
item.description: Robotic-assisted minimally invasive cardiac surgery offers the potential to perform off-pump beating heart procedures without cardiopulmonary bypass, but active closed-loop algorithmic motion compensation, as distinct from image-stabilization, motion-tracking, and mechanical-stabilization approaches that have seen limited clinical use, has not yet entered human clinical trials despite two decades of research. This scoping review, conducted using the PRISMA-ScR framework, addresses three...

item.title: A novel bacterial symbiont in the seaweed Gracilaria tenuistipitata and its promising anti-inflammatory and antiproliferative potential in relation to special secreted metabolites
item.description: Marine macroalgae host compositionally complex microbiomes that constitute an evolutionarily refined, yet largely unexplored source of structurally diverse natural products. Thus, the bioactivities of the algae may be related to those of their associated microorganisms. Here we describe the discovery of strain S.100, an endophytic bacterium isolated from the red alga Gracilaria tenuistipitata and displaying remarkable anti-inflammatory and antiproliferative activities, through a primary...

item.title: Integrative single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis identify R-loop-associated gene signatures driving immune-inflammatory networks in acute pancreatitis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight R-loop-associated gene signatures and functionally validated Myl12a as plausible candidates for dissecting AP pathogenesis. This work provides mechanistic clues for AP-related immune-inflammatory, which need further researches to verify.

item.title: A NET-associated immunothrombotic phenotype is associated with coronary no-reflow and myocardial injury after primary PCI in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: a real-world translational cohort
item.description: CONCLUSION: A NET-IP was linked to impaired coronary reperfusion and myocardial injury after primary PCI in STEMI. The findings support NET-associated immunothrombosis as a clinically measurable immune phenotype but do not establish direct NET burden, causal mediation, or immediate clinical treatment guidance.

item.title: Bioelectrical impedance-derived body composition and systemic therapy outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: BIA-assessed skeletal muscle reserve and visceral adiposity were associated with outcomes during ICI-based therapy in men with NSCLC. Higher SMI and lower VFI identified a more favorable clinical profile. Prospective validation is warranted to define the role of BIA-based body-composition assessment in host-related risk stratification during systemic therapy.

item.title: Impact of immersive virtual reality and transcranial direct current stimulation over the parietal cortex on motor response
item.description: Immersive virtual reality (IVR) provides interactive and engaging environments to stimulate motor learning and neuroplasticity. Combining IVR with transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) may further enhance these effects by modulating activity in targeted brain areas. We investigated the effects of a 5-day IVR game-training (Beat Saber game for PS4) alone or combined with sham or anodal tDCS over the left posterior parietal cortex, a key structure for visuospatial processing and motor...

item.title: Effect of rosuvastatin and ezetimibe therapy on LDL-cholesterol reduction and non-invasive arterial injury markers in children with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia: a prospective, open-label, randomized study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Rosuvastatin achieved greater LDL-C reduction than ezetimibe in children with FH, without difference in safety and tolerability profiles. Arterial injury markers correlated mainly with age and anthropometry, and their short-term changes were not treatment-related, likely due to limited power and the short follow-up.

item.title: Apathy-depression overlap: unmasking hidden disability profiles in multiple sclerosis
item.description: BACKGROUND: Multiple sclerosis (MS), the leading cause of non-traumatic neurological disability in young adults, features heterogeneous motor and non-motor symptoms including fatigue, apathy and depression. Although fatigue and depression are well-studied in MS disability progression, to date, the independent and combined contributions of apathy, fatigue and depression to neurological disability remain unexplored.

item.title: High sperm DNA fragmentation is associated with increased embryonic chromosomal abnormality: a retrospective study of 8 years involving 5637 couples undergoing ART
item.description: STUDY QUESTION: Does sperm DNA fragmentation impair blastocyst chromosomal integrity?

item.title: Electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy-guided three-dimensional conformal microwave ablation for unresectable peripheral high-risk pulmonary nodules: a mid-term assessment with no real-time intraoperative CT/cone-beam computed tomography guidance
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: ENB-DCMA serves as a safe and feasible minimally invasive therapeutic option for patients with high-risk pulmonary nodules. Further multicenter prospective trials are required to verify its long-term outcomes and broader clinical popularization value.

item.title: Surgery that looks like transcatheter aortic valve implantation: the transaxillary concept for minimally invasive aortic valve replacement in 1,848 consecutive patients
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Across 1,848 consecutive procedures, TxA MICS-AVR showed excellent reproducibility and safety. As long-term evidence increasingly supports surgical valve replacement in patients with extended life expectancy, TxA uniquely combines durable surgery with a cosmetic result comparable to transcatheter therapy, offering a scalable and strategically relevant platform for contemporary aortic valve care.

item.title: Extremely rare primary tracheal hyalinizing clear cell carcinoma: two case reports
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Primary tracheal HCCC should be considered in the differential diagnosis of tracheal clear cell tumors. Accurate diagnosis requires integration of histomorphology, immunohistochemistry, and molecular testing for EWSR1 alterations. Complete surgical resection with negative margins appears to be an effective treatment for localized disease. Because late recurrence or metastasis may occur and evidence remains limited, prolonged postoperative surveillance and further accumulation of...

item.title: Response to van Boxtel et al., 'Testing errors in measuring the effective orifice diameter as a new sizing parameter of surgical valve prostheses'
item.description: No abstract

item.title: When inclusive leadership meets supervisory interaction pressure: explaining innovative behavior among public employees
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Public organizations increasingly depend on employees to identify service failures and implement improvements, yet immediate supervisors combine developmental support with evaluative authority. Drawing on job demands-resources theory and integrating psychological contract and public service motivation research, this study examines how inclusive leadership is associated with innovative behavior and when supervisory interaction pressure constrains this relationship.

item.title: Adjuvant alectinib versus crizotinib in completely resected ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer: a real-world retrospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort of patients with completely resected ALK-positive NSCLC, adjuvant alectinib was associated with longer DFS, improved BMFS, and a more favorable safety profile than crizotinib. These findings are broadly consistent with the benefit of adjuvant alectinib observed in the phase III ALINA trial and support alectinib as the preferred adjuvant ALK-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) option over crizotinib. Further validation in larger multicenter real-world or...

item.title: Nutritional and Sensory Evaluation of Complementary Foods Developed From Staple Grains and Dried Dagaa Fish (Stolothrissa tanganicae)
item.description: Plant-based complementary foods commonly consumed in South-Kivu are often deficient in protein and essential micronutrients, contributing to undernutrition among young children. This study developed fish-enriched complementary flours and evaluated their proximate composition, sensory quality, acceptability, and storability. Three composite flours were formulated: a control complementary flour (CCF, no fish) and two enriched formulations containing 40% (ECF1) and 20% (ECF2) dried dagaa. Proximate...

item.title: Multi-cohort validation of BRAF-PTPRT co-mutation as a predictor of favorable immunotherapy response in melanoma
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: BRAF-PTPRT co-mutation is a robust, cross-cohort predictive biomarker for ICB response in melanoma. A simple risk score integrating co-mutation and TMB further improves patient stratification. Routine testing of both genes may guide immunotherapy decisions.

item.title: Sargassum soluble dietary fiber alleviates oxidative stress and gut microbiota dysbiosis to prevent inflammatory bowel disease in C57BL/6 mice
item.description: CONCLUSION: BL-SDF alleviates intestinal inflammation by enhancing antioxidant activities and modulating gut microbiota, suggesting that fermented Sargassum SDF may serve as a dietary strategy for preventing inflammatory bowel disease. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

item.title: Whole-Genome Sequencing-Based Characterization and Antimicrobial Resistance Analysis of Shiga Toxin-Producing Escherichia coli Isolated from Retail Meat Products
item.description: Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC), a zoonotic foodborne pathogen, has become a critical global public health issue. This study investigates molecular traits and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) mechanisms of STEC strains derived from retail meat products sourced from domestic production in Liaocheng city, Shandong province, China, to inform health risk assessment. Using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), phenotypic AMR testing, and whole-genome sequencing (WGS),...

item.title: Effect of implantable collamer lens on biometric measurements and intraocular lens power calculation formulas
item.description: CONCLUSION: ICL implantation alters biometric measurements and theoretically predicted Δ-pSEQ; although these changes are statistically significant, their clinical significance is negligible. While incorrect ACD segmentation is common, it is unlikely to substantially affect the theoretical calculation results.

item.title: Performance Evaluation of Dry Chemical Colorimetry for Plasma Ammonia Detection on the VITROS 350 Chemistry System
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study validates the reliability of the VITROS dry chemistry system for routine plasma ammonia testing. It provides clinical laboratories with a robust framework for method selection and establishes a framework for future external quality assessment (EQA) based on dry chemistry colorimetry.

item.title: Stereocontrolled Assembly of Benzofulvenes and Dihydronaphthalenes via a Tandem Chromium Catalyzed NHK/Cyclization Cascade
item.description: Functionalized benzofulvenes and dihydronaphthalenes are privileged scaffolds with profound utility in medicinal chemistry and materials science. However, their modular synthesis is often bottlenecked by a reliance on complex, pre-functionalized precursors and a persistent challenge to control exocyclic E/Z stereochemistry. item.title: Reaction Energy Landscape of Propane Oxidative Dehydrogenation on Liquid Boron Oxide-Germinated Catalytic Sites in the Presence of Dioxygen: An Orbitals-Driven Mechanistic Study
item.description: Recently, boron-based catalysts have gained significant attention for the oxidative dehydrogenation of propane into propene and ethene. In this study, we present an electronic-level understanding of propane oxidation via a triplet dioxygen molecule over liquid boron oxide motifs, including cyclic B-O-B sites (8-, 6-, and 4-membered rings) and edge B-OH and B-B sites. Our computations reveal that cyclic B-O-B and edge B-OH motifs exhibit higher activation barriers for C(3)H(6) (55-71 kcal...

item.title: Molecular Entropies of Conformationally Flexible, Gas-Phase Forms of Clinical Drugs: A Black-Box Approach Versus Systematic Sampling
item.description: The results of the exhaustive conformational sampling are contrasted with metadynamics-based CREST simulations for a set of 13 gas-phase forms of clinical drug molecules retrieved from the CD25 dataset. [Chem. Sci. 2021, 12 (19), 6551] The GFN1- and GFN2-xTB methods complement each other in the identification of the most stable conformer. The GFN-FF performs worse due to fundamental differences between the force field and the density functional theory (DFT) potential energy surfaces....

item.title: The RcDREB1E-RcMYB28 module improves drought tolerance in Rosa chinensis via RcLAR/RcCORA1-mediated proanthocyanidin biosynthesis and stress responses
item.description: Drought is widely recognized as one of the most severe abiotic stresses limiting plant growth and productivity. Proanthocyanidins (PAs), as key functional secondary metabolites, are central to enhancing plant tolerance to abiotic stresses. Nevertheless, the specific mechanisms underlying PA-mediated drought resistance in rose remain largely unclear. Herein, we demonstrate that drought-induced PA accumulation constitutes a conserved evolutionary mechanism across the plant kingdom, ranging from...

item.title: Inflammasome-Related Transcriptomic Profiles in Periodontitis and Peri-Implantitis Reveal a Shared Inflammatory Framework: A Cross-Sectional Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Periodontitis and peri-implantitis share a substantial inflammasome-related host-response framework. Rather than revealing a distinct inflammasome program, peri-implantitis exhibits a largely overlapping molecular profile that occurs within a clinically more severe and structurally more disrupted lesion environment. These findings suggest that the biological distinction between the two diseases may lie less in pathway identity than in the tissue context in which a shared...

item.title: Overcoming Detection Lag in a Cryptic Panzootic: Chytrid Invasion Linked to Historically Enigmatic Amphibian Declines in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest
item.description: As human activity accelerates the spread of pathogens and other invasive species, reconstructing the cryptic early dynamics of undetected invasions has become a central challenge in disease ecology and invasion biology. Here, we leverage museum specimens to reconstruct the invasion of Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd), a fungal panzootic driving global amphibian biodiversity loss, across historically enigmatic declines in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest. item.title: Indium Phosphide Quantum Dots in Biomedicine: Photophysics, Bio-Nano Interactions, and Emerging Imaging and Therapeutic Platforms
item.description: Indium phosphide (InP) quantum dots (QDs) have emerged as promising cadmium-free semiconductor nanomaterials with considerable potential for biomedical applications due to their tunable optical properties, high photostability, and favorable emission characteristics. In this review, the fundamental photophysical properties of InP QDs are first discussed to clarify the mechanisms governing their optical behavior and emission tunability. Subsequently, the key factors influencing their interactions...

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Navigating School While Living With Cystic Fibrosis: Barriers and Support Strategies From the Patient and Family Perspective
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study identifies common school-related issues faced by PwCF and caregivers that warrant targeted and proactive attention to support academic achievement and wellbeing. Caregivers and PwCF feel comfortable addressing school-related issues with CF care teams and prefer the care team to initiate conversations about school. Study results emphasize the benefit of having a centralized and comprehensive CF-specific repository that can be easily accessed by care teams to proactively...

item.description: γ-Aminobutyric acid (GABA) is an amino acid with a variety of biological functions and is now becoming an essential food ingredient. In this work, a GABA-producing lactic acid bacterium was isolated from godeulppaegi kimchi and characterized by phenotypic, biochemical and molecular parameters. The isolate was identified as FBL-3, which produced acid colonies in MRS agar containing CaCO(3) and L-glutamic acid, was Gram positive, catalase-negative and rod-shaped, and had 99.1% similarity to...

item.title: Computed Tomography-Derived Psoas Muscle Quantity, Attenuation, and 1 Year Mortality in Venovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation
item.description: Computed tomography (CT)-derived skeletal muscle characteristics may provide prognostic information in patients receiving venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV ECMO), but the relative contributions of muscle quantity and attenuation remain uncertain. We retrospectively studied adults who received VV ECMO for severe respiratory failure between 2014 and 2023 and underwent abdominal CT within 48 h before ECMO initiation. Psoas muscle index (PMI) and attenuation were measured using an...

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Engineering of bacterial outer membrane vesicles for biotechnological applications
item.description: Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) are spherical, nano-sized proteoliposomes naturally secreted by Gram-negative bacteria. By incorporating parental membrane components and encapsulating diverse cellular cargos, OMVs function as potent mediators of biological communication. Despite inherent challenges, including low production yields, heterogeneous composition, and stochastic cargo loading, OMVs hold immense promise across broad biotechnological landscapes. In this review, we examine current...

item.title: Effects of metal ions on amyloid liquid-liquid phase separation and liquid-to-solid phase transition
item.description: Metal ions have emerged as critical factors influencing biomolecular phase separation and are increasingly implicated in the formation, maturation, and pathological transformation of condensates associated with amyloidogenic proteins. Recent studies have shown that metal ions can affect liquid-liquid phase separation and liquid-to-solid phase transition through multiple mechanisms, including electrostatic interactions, direct metal coordination, intermolecular bridging, and metal-induced...

item.title: Ordered Anti-Restacking Three-Dimensional Ti3C2Tx MXene Networks on Silicon Microcone Arrays via Template-Directed Assembly for Highly Efficient Room-Temperature Ammonia Sensing
item.description: The realization of room-temperature, low-power chemiresistive ammonia (NH3) sensors is highly desirable yet remains a formidable challenge, primarily hindered by the high activation energy of conventional metal oxides and the severe nanosheet restacking of emerging 2D MXene. Here, we propose a morphology-templated assembly strategy to construct an antirestacking, highly accessible 3D Ti3C2Tx MXene sensing network using ordered silicon microcone arrays as 3D scaffolds. This architectural design...

item.description: Chiral-lattice degrees of freedom can offer novel chirality-selective functionalities for thermotronic applications. Chiral phonons, which carry both heat and angular momentum, can arise from broken chiral degeneracy in phonon bands or from angular momentum transfer from photons or spins. Here, we demonstrate a nanoscale chirality-selective phonon transport based on a simple heterostructure of ferromagnetic [Co/Pt] multilayers and insulating chiral α-SiO(2). Using magneto-optic thermometry, we...

item.title: Silicate fertilizer mitigates methane emissions from rice paddies by enriching Burkholderia to modulate microbial interactions
item.description: Methane emissions from rice paddies are a major source of greenhouse gases, and silicate fertilizer (SF) derived from blast furnace slag has emerged as an environmentally friendly amendment that reduces methane release. SF modifies the soil redox environment by supplying electron acceptors such as iron, but the microbial mechanisms underlying methane mitigation remain unclear. Here, we combined metagenomic profiling, microbial isolation, and greenhouse experiments to show that SF consistently...

item.title: Position Over Composition: Positional Isomerism Enables Encapsulation-Independent Intrinsic Stability in a Conjugated Polymer
item.description: Conjugated polymers derive their optoelectronic function from π-delocalization. However, this feature renders them intrinsically susceptible to photochemical degradation. Here, we show that intrinsic stability can be altered without changing chemical composition by repositioning side chains. In polydiphenylacetylene derivatives, shifting substituents from the para to the meta position increases photostability by more than fivefold. This stability hierarchy, driven by positional isomerism rather...

item.title: Patterns of base chromosome numbers, genome size and rDNA loci evolution in the genus Capsicum (Solanaceae)
item.description: The size, organization and dynamics of the evolution of plant genomes vary widely among and within evolutionary lineages. The relatively small genus Capsicum provides an excellent system for studying genome evolution because all the species are diploid and possess one of two base chromosome numbers (x = 12 or 13). Here, we report chromosome numbers, genome sizes, and numbers of 5S and 35S rDNA loci for 24 Capsicum taxa representing eight of the nine currently recognized clades and one outgroup...

item.title: Chemical Functionality Engineering of Anti-Solvent Additives for Photostable Perovskite Solar Cells
item.description: Metal-halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieve high power-conversion efficiencies but remain susceptible to photo-induced degradation caused by mobile ions and phase segregation. Here, we investigate positional isomers of pyridine-carboxylic acid, namely pyridine-2-carboxylic acid (2-PC) and pyridine-4-carboxylic acid (4-PC), as anti-solvent additives to clarify how functional-group orientation governs defect passivation and photo-induced degradation. Both additives improve film morphology...

item.title: Prevalence of Sarcopenia in Korean Adults Based on the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia 2025 Criteria: Analysis of the 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
item.description: CONCLUSION: Application of the AWGS 2025 BMI-adjusted criteria identifies a substantial proportion of Korean older adults at risk of sarcopenia, with women aged ≥ 80 years particularly vulnerable. The divergence between BIA and DEXA measurements in very old adults suggests that measurement modality should be carefully considered in clinical practice. These findings provide timely evidence for public health planning as Korea enters a super-aged society.

item.title: Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin Limits Glucocorticoid-Induced Muscle Wasting by Preserving Estrogen-Dependent Repression of Catabolic Signaling
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: SHBG acts as a promoter of estrogen bioavailability that coordinates a protective endocrine crosstalk, counteracting GR-driven catabolism in female skeletal muscle. These findings identify SHBG as a key metabolic determinant and a promising therapeutic target to prevent corticosteroid-induced muscle wasting.

item.title: The Receptor for Advanced Glycation End Products: Regulation and Implications in Metabolic Diseases
item.description: Receptor for advanced glycation end-products (RAGE) was originally identified as a receptor for advanced glycation end-products; however, it can also bind a broader range of damage-associated molecular patterns, including S100 proteins, high mobility group box 1, and amyloid-β. item.title: Translational modelling of human microglia from cultures to chimeras
item.description: Microglia play a crucial role in maintaining homeostasis of the central nervous system, whereas their dysfunction is implicated in the pathogenesis of various neurological diseases. Nevertheless, interspecific genetic differences pose challenges to translating findings from conventional rodent models. item.title: Impact of calcium fluoride loading on the physicochemical and antibacterial properties of different pit and fissure sealants
item.description: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of incorporating calcium fluoride (CaF₂) particles into different pit and fissure sealants on their physicochemical properties, fluoride release, and antibacterial activity.

item.title: Comparison of Integrated Versus Sequential Artificial Intelligence-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis Systems in Breast Ultrasound: A Prospective Pilot Study on Examination Time, Reproducibility, and Diagnostic Performance
item.description: CONCLUSION: Integrated and sequential AI-CAD systems showed complementary strengths in breast US. Integrated AI-CAD favored shorter examination time and higher sensitivity, whereas sequential AI-CAD favored higher specificity, with reproducibility differing according to lesion type.

item.title: Health Policy for Obesity and Metabolic Syndrome in Asian Health Systems: Three Design Principles, Three Binding Constraints, and the Governance That Decides between Them
item.description: CONCLUSION: Obesity policy in Asia requires governance mechanisms built into its design: a permanent inter-agency body with protected funding, legal safeguards against industry interference, and mandatory equity audits with independent monitoring. Access to incretin-based medications belongs in the same framework; otherwise, these drugs may widen regional inequities.

item.title: Evaluation of Costal Cartilage Calcification Using Plain Radiographic Images
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Routine rib series imaging should be considered even in younger candidates to optimize donor site selection and avoid unexpected intraoperative findings.

item.title: Fibromyalgia Subgroups Identified Using Model-Based Clustering: Results from UK Biobank
item.description: Fibromyalgia (FM) is a heterogeneous chronic condition with wide variability in symptom burden, psychosocial distress, and functional impact. This study aimed to identify latent FM subgroups reflecting multidimensional patient profiles using comprehensive biopsychosocial variables and model-based clustering methods within UK Biobank. item.title: Initial complete local therapy without systemic therapy versus systemic-therapy-based management in selected patients with oligometastatic renal cell carcinoma: a matched comparative study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this selected post-nephrectomy cohort, an initial complete-local-therapy strategy without ST was associated with higher OS and CSS than heterogeneous, predominantly TKI-based ST management, although PFS and DMFS were similar. Given the nonrandomized treatment allocation and residual biological selection, these findings are hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as evidence of superiority over contemporary ICI-based therapy.
